Alain Prost became the first driver to successfully defend his World Championship since Jack Brabham in 1960 following a season that climaxed in a classic three-way title fight at the final round in Adelaide. Prost appeared to have little chance against the powerful Williams-Hondas of Nigel Mansell and the pre-season favourite Nelson Piquet. But with just eighteen laps remaining and the title in his grasp, Mansell suffered a spectacular 180 mph puncture that ended his hopes. Piquet was then forced to change tyres as a precaution, handing the race and title to a surprised but ecstatic Prost.

Williams’ year had begun badly when team founder Frank Williams was paralysed in a road accident. But Mansell was a revelation once the season started. He drove with newly found maturity and speed, winning four times and overshadowing his more illustrious new team-mate.

However, as the Williams team-mates fought a tense battle for supremacy, Prost also won four races and finished in the points on all but three occasions. Although his McLaren was at times no match for the Williams (he was a lapped third at Brands Hatch), Prost’s consistency won out over the full season.

Ayrton Senna was the fourth major title protagonist. He beat Mansell by half a car-length in a dash to the finish line at Spain’s new venue at Jerez. Another victory on the streets of Detroit kept him in the championship hunt until the end of the European season. Senna qualified on pole position and led half of the season’s events, but ultimately his Lotus-Renault could not match his pace.

Gerhard Berger scored a first victory in Mexico after several impressive performances in the powerful Benetton-BMW. While the Goodyear-equipped cars all made tyre stops, Berger ran without pitting to give Pirelli a rare success. Teo Fabi qualified on pole twice for Benetton, but never led a lap.

This was also the year of the low-line Brabham BT55. In order to reduce frontal area and lower the centre of gravity, the car’s BMW engine lay almost flat in the chassis and was mated to a new compact, seven-speed Weismann gearbox. However, the car suffered gearbox and overheating problems and failed to impress. Tragedy also touched the team when Elio de Angelis was killed in May while testing a BT55 at Circuit Paul Ricard.

Jacques Lafitte also suffered career-ending injuries at the start of the British GP – the very race in which he equalled Graham Hill’s long-standing record for Grand Prix starts. Keke Rosberg also retired from Formula 1 after a disappointing year at McLaren.

Finally, F1 held a race in communist Europe for the first time at the new Hungaroring outside Budapest, where a huge crowd witnessed a great race between Senna and Piquet.

Alain Prost became the first driver to successfully defend his World Championship since Jack Brabham in 1960 following a season that climaxed in a classic three-way title fight at the final round in Adelaide. Prost appeared to have little chance against the powerful Williams-Hondas of Nigel Mansell and the pre-season favourite Nelson Piquet. But with just eighteen laps remaining and the title in his grasp, Mansell suffered a spectacular 180 mph puncture that ended his hopes. Piquet was then forced to change tyres as a precaution, handing the race and title to a surprised but ecstatic Prost.

Williams’ year had begun badly when team founder Frank Williams was paralysed in a road accident. But Mansell was a revelation once the season started. He drove with newly found maturity and speed, winning four times and overshadowing his more illustrious new team-mate.

However, as the Williams team-mates fought a tense battle for supremacy, Prost also won four races and finished in the points on all but three occasions. Although his McLaren was at times no match for the Williams (he was a lapped third at Brands Hatch), Prost’s consistency won out over the full season.

Ayrton Senna was the fourth major title protagonist. He beat Mansell by half a car-length in a dash to the finish line at Spain’s new venue at Jerez. Another victory on the streets of Detroit kept him in the championship hunt until the end of the European season. Senna qualified on pole position and led half of the season’s events, but ultimately his Lotus-Renault could not match his pace.

Gerhard Berger scored a first victory in Mexico after several impressive performances in the powerful Benetton-BMW. While the Goodyear-equipped cars all made tyre stops, Berger ran without pitting to give Pirelli a rare success. Teo Fabi qualified on pole twice for Benetton, but never led a lap.

This was also the year of the low-line Brabham BT55. In order to reduce frontal area and lower the centre of gravity, the car’s BMW engine lay almost flat in the chassis and was mated to a new compact, seven-speed Weismann gearbox. However, the car suffered gearbox and overheating problems and failed to impress. Tragedy also touched the team when Elio de Angelis was killed in May while testing a BT55 at Circuit Paul Ricard.

Jacques Lafitte also suffered career-ending injuries at the start of the British GP – the very race in which he equalled Graham Hill’s long-standing record for Grand Prix starts. Keke Rosberg also retired from Formula 1 after a disappointing year at McLaren.

Finally, F1 held a race in communist Europe for the first time at the new Hungaroring outside Budapest, where a huge crowd witnessed a great race between Senna and Piquet.

# Grand Prix Gold: French GP 1986

## Nigel Mansell recorded his third win of the Formula 1 World Championship season with a consumate Sunday afternoon drive at the French Grand Prix on a day when only national hero Alain Prost offered any real challenge to the Williams man

[Nigel Roebuck](https://www.autosport.com/info/about-us/all/236510/)

Published:18 Aug 2011, 18:26

On Sunday, Nigel Mansell guaranteed chaos on the roads of Kent this coming weekend. For the first time in a decade British spectators will go to their home grand prix to cheer on one of their own as a truly serous contender for the world championship. Mansell has now won three of the previous four races, and this one he laid claim to in the opening seconds. Only Alain Prost offered true opposition.

Ayrton Senna took pole, but crashed early. Nelson Piquet and Keke Rosberg were thereabouts, but not truly in the picture. Poor tyre stops did nothing to help the Ligiers, although both took points. The Ferraris were not a factor. Patrick Head correctly surmised that two tyre stops were the right policy for Williams-Honda and left the rest to his driver, who made no mistake. It was another drive from the top drawer.

# Grand Prix Gold: French GP 1986

## Nigel Mansell recorded his third win of the Formula 1 World Championship season with a consumate Sunday afternoon drive at the French Grand Prix on a day when only national hero Alain Prost offered any real challenge to the Williams man

[Nigel Roebuck](https://www.autosport.com/info/about-us/all/236510/)

Published:18 Aug 2011, 18:26

On Sunday, Nigel Mansell guaranteed chaos on the roads of Kent this coming weekend. For the first time in a decade British spectators will go to their home grand prix to cheer on one of their own as a truly serous contender for the world championship. Mansell has now won three of the previous four races, and this one he laid claim to in the opening seconds. Only Alain Prost offered true opposition.

Ayrton Senna took pole, but crashed early. Nelson Piquet and Keke Rosberg were thereabouts, but not truly in the picture. Poor tyre stops did nothing to help the Ligiers, although both took points. The Ferraris were not a factor. Patrick Head correctly surmised that two tyre stops were the right policy for Williams-Honda and left the rest to his driver, who made no mistake. It was another drive from the top drawer.

# 1986 French Grand Prix

July 5, 2015[1986](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/category/1986/), [France](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/category/france/), [Race Reports](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/category/race-reports/)[1986](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/tag/1986/), [France](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/tag/france/), [Paul Ricard](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/tag/paul-ricard/), [Races](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/tag/races/)[Matt](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/author/johnthebloggist/ "View all posts by Matt")

**[![Image 2: 220px-Paul_Ricard_1986](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/220px-paul_ricard_1986.jpg?w=604)](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/220px-paul_ricard_1986.jpg)Circuit Paul Ricard  
 6 July 1986**

The Grand Prix circus returned to the Paul Ricard circuit in the south of France for the first time since Elio de Angelis’ fatal accident, and a decision had been made to cut out the high-speed corner where the Brabham had crashed, at the end of the long Mistral straight, using the racing school track to curtail Mistral and shorten the circuit overall.

FISA had also announced some radical plans for the future. Turbocharged engines, which had been compulsory in 1986 for the first time, were now to be banned in the interests both of safety and of curtailing spiralling costs. Rather than an outright ban for 1987, however, it was decided to “phase out” the turbo engines. In 1987, turbocharged engines would be restricted to four bars (ie 4x atmospheric pressure) of boost and a 1l engine, while a new category of 3.5l normally-aspirated engine would be allowed. For 1988, then, the turbo [![Image 3: FRA Palmer](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-palmer.jpg?w=300&h=201)](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-palmer.jpg)boost would be further restricted to 2.5 bars, and an outright ban from 1989 onwards. The FIA hoped that the boost restrictions would encourage existing teams to convert early and new teams to enter, as well as easing the transition.

In team news, Patrick Tambay was back in action for Team Haas Lola, along with his new race engineer, Adrian Newey, hired away from the March IndyCar project.

Despite the Ligier team’s good showing at Detroitl local hopes rested largely on Alain Prost in his McLaren, but the Woking cars had traditionally focussed on race results rather than qualifying and Prost duly put his red and white car fifth on the grid, just behind Arnoux’s Ligier. At the front was Senna’s Lotus, with Mansell alongside and Piquet in third. Alboreto put his Ferrari in an encouraging 6th place, followed by Berger and Fabi in the Benettons and Johansson rounding out the top ten in the second Ferrari.The two Osellas again brought up the rear, with Berg the _Laterne Rouge_ for the grid.

[![Image 4: FRA Mansell](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-mansell.jpg?w=604)](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-mansell.jpg)Alboreto’s encouraging qualifying came to naught as he stalled on the grid and Piquet got away slowly, while Mansell stormed away into the lead ahead of Senna, Arnoux, Berger, Prost and Dumfries (who had got a cracking start from 12th in the second Lotus). Rosberg got past Dumfries during the first lap, while Johansson came in before the end of the lap for the Ferrari mechanics to take the back off his car and poke at the engine. It looked like it was going to be another long, frustrating race for Maranello.

A couple of laps later, with Jones already retired, Andrea de Cesaris was removed with an explosive turbo failure, and on the following lap, the fourth, Ayrton Senna skidded on the resultant oil slick and put his Lotus into the tyre barrier and out of the race. Mansell thus led with an increased margin, with Arnoux now second but gaining as Mansell was already encountering backmarkers, with Warwick, Rothengatter and Johansson all having made pit stops in the early stages. Behind Arnoux, Berger was now third, but holding up the two McLarens of Prost and Rosberg.

Prost got by Berger in traffic on lap 5, just as Johansson came in again, this time to retire with turbo issues, and Rosberg followed his team-mate past the Benetton shortly afterwards. Prost was soon up behind Arnoux and wasted little time in muscling his way past his compatriot and former Renault team-mate on lap 16, with Rosberg following through two laps later.

Advertisement

Prost was now up to second, with just over 4.4s between him and the leading Williams. Unable to keep up, Arnoux pitted for tyres at the end of lap 18, but undid a lot of the team’s good work when, on rejoining, he was forced to stamp on the brakes in order to avoid colliding with Tambay. Mansell, meanwhile, had pulled out another half-second over Prost as he continued carving through traffic, while Rosberg was being thoroughly left behind by the pair of them and his third place was coming

under threat from Piquet. The Brazilian made a (sub-9 second) tyre stop on lap 22, just as Berger collided with Danner’s Arrows and removed himself from proceedings. Danner called in for repairs but was able to continue.

Two laps later, with Prost having eaten up the gap, Mansell peeled off into the pits himself. The Williams team put him out in just 8.12 seconds, rejoining third just ahead of Jacques Laffite, who came in for his own stop a couple of laps later, while Mansell set about catching the McLarens, reeling off a series of Fastest Laps. Rosberg was next to pit for tyres, rejoining [![Image 5: FRA Patrese](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-patrese.jpg?w=300&h=204)](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-patrese.jpg)fourth, which promoted Mansell to second and Piquet to third, but Prost continued racing, even after a big lock-up under braking on lap 31 which must have flat-spotted his already old tyres. With a 12-second lead over Mansell decreasing all the time, he surely couldn’t leave it much longer if he was to retain his lead. Eventually he did, rejoining second, some 16 seconds behind Mansell with Piquet rapidly gaining and Rosberg behind the Williams.

As Prost made his way through traffic, he was balked by Alboreto, himself trying to better his position as he diced with Tambay. Prost made his way through but as Piquet did so, Rosberg pulled off a daring move around the outside and took third place. The Brazilian’s car began dropping back almost immediately with electrical gremlins while Rosberg nearly wiped off a front wheel trying a similarly ambitious move to lap Patrese’s Brabham. Phillippe Streiff’s Tyrrell pulled off in flames on lap 43 – the French driver hopped out with no apparent ill effects, but the fire resisted all attempts by the marshals to snuff it out with hand extinguishers and a fire engine had to come and hose it down.

Mansell continued serenely on in the lead, until he came in for his second tyre stop on lap 50 which dropped him to second, emerging just in front of Rosberg’s McLaren. On fresh rubber, he quickly pulled away from his 1985 team-mate but the question was whether the new tyres would make him fast enough to catch and pass the one-stopping Prost before the end of the race. He started well, tearing chunks out of Prost’s lead over the next laps, and putting up a new fastest lap some two seconds faster than the previous one. By lap 57 he was right behind Prost and as they came round to begin lap 58, Mansell breezed past on at the first corner. Prost managed to stick with Mansell as the pair carved through traffic, but once out on [![Image 6: FRA Finish](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-finish.jpg?w=604)](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-finish.jpg)clear track, the Williams quickly pulled away.

And that was more or less how it finished; during the closing stages of the race, Piquet had an improvement in pace and reeled in Rosberg, making his way past the Finn just a few laps from the chequered flag. So Mansell took the win, with Prost second, Piquet third and Rosberg fourth, and the Ligiers of Arnoux and Laffite coming in fifth and sixth to round out the points.

[![Image 7: FRA Podium Mansell](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-podium-mansell.jpg?w=194&h=300)](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-podium-mansell.jpg)Mansell’s win put him second in the title race, just a point behind Prost; both overtaking the unfortunate Senna. In the constructors’ stakes, Williams extended their lead over McLaren thanks to Piquet’s heroics in the closing stages.

# 1986 French Grand Prix

July 5, 2015[1986](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/category/1986/), [France](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/category/france/), [Race Reports](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/category/race-reports/)[1986](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/tag/1986/), [France](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/tag/france/), [Paul Ricard](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/tag/paul-ricard/), [Races](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/tag/races/)[Matt](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/author/johnthebloggist/ "View all posts by Matt")

**[![Image 2: 220px-Paul_Ricard_1986](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/220px-paul_ricard_1986.jpg?w=604)](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/220px-paul_ricard_1986.jpg)Circuit Paul Ricard  
 6 July 1986**

The Grand Prix circus returned to the Paul Ricard circuit in the south of France for the first time since Elio de Angelis’ fatal accident, and a decision had been made to cut out the high-speed corner where the Brabham had crashed, at the end of the long Mistral straight, using the racing school track to curtail Mistral and shorten the circuit overall.

FISA had also announced some radical plans for the future. Turbocharged engines, which had been compulsory in 1986 for the first time, were now to be banned in the interests both of safety and of curtailing spiralling costs. Rather than an outright ban for 1987, however, it was decided to “phase out” the turbo engines. In 1987, turbocharged engines would be restricted to four bars (ie 4x atmospheric pressure) of boost and a 1l engine, while a new category of 3.5l normally-aspirated engine would be allowed. For 1988, then, the turbo [![Image 3: FRA Palmer](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-palmer.jpg?w=300&h=201)](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-palmer.jpg)boost would be further restricted to 2.5 bars, and an outright ban from 1989 onwards. The FIA hoped that the boost restrictions would encourage existing teams to convert early and new teams to enter, as well as easing the transition.

In team news, Patrick Tambay was back in action for Team Haas Lola, along with his new race engineer, Adrian Newey, hired away from the March IndyCar project.

Despite the Ligier team’s good showing at Detroitl local hopes rested largely on Alain Prost in his McLaren, but the Woking cars had traditionally focussed on race results rather than qualifying and Prost duly put his red and white car fifth on the grid, just behind Arnoux’s Ligier. At the front was Senna’s Lotus, with Mansell alongside and Piquet in third. Alboreto put his Ferrari in an encouraging 6th place, followed by Berger and Fabi in the Benettons and Johansson rounding out the top ten in the second Ferrari.The two Osellas again brought up the rear, with Berg the _Laterne Rouge_ for the grid.

[![Image 4: FRA Mansell](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-mansell.jpg?w=604)](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-mansell.jpg)Alboreto’s encouraging qualifying came to naught as he stalled on the grid and Piquet got away slowly, while Mansell stormed away into the lead ahead of Senna, Arnoux, Berger, Prost and Dumfries (who had got a cracking start from 12th in the second Lotus). Rosberg got past Dumfries during the first lap, while Johansson came in before the end of the lap for the Ferrari mechanics to take the back off his car and poke at the engine. It looked like it was going to be another long, frustrating race for Maranello.

A couple of laps later, with Jones already retired, Andrea de Cesaris was removed with an explosive turbo failure, and on the following lap, the fourth, Ayrton Senna skidded on the resultant oil slick and put his Lotus into the tyre barrier and out of the race. Mansell thus led with an increased margin, with Arnoux now second but gaining as Mansell was already encountering backmarkers, with Warwick, Rothengatter and Johansson all having made pit stops in the early stages. Behind Arnoux, Berger was now third, but holding up the two McLarens of Prost and Rosberg.

Prost got by Berger in traffic on lap 5, just as Johansson came in again, this time to retire with turbo issues, and Rosberg followed his team-mate past the Benetton shortly afterwards. Prost was soon up behind Arnoux and wasted little time in muscling his way past his compatriot and former Renault team-mate on lap 16, with Rosberg following through two laps later.

Advertisement

Prost was now up to second, with just over 4.4s between him and the leading Williams. Unable to keep up, Arnoux pitted for tyres at the end of lap 18, but undid a lot of the team’s good work when, on rejoining, he was forced to stamp on the brakes in order to avoid colliding with Tambay. Mansell, meanwhile, had pulled out another half-second over Prost as he continued carving through traffic, while Rosberg was being thoroughly left behind by the pair of them and his third place was coming

under threat from Piquet. The Brazilian made a (sub-9 second) tyre stop on lap 22, just as Berger collided with Danner’s Arrows and removed himself from proceedings. Danner called in for repairs but was able to continue.

Two laps later, with Prost having eaten up the gap, Mansell peeled off into the pits himself. The Williams team put him out in just 8.12 seconds, rejoining third just ahead of Jacques Laffite, who came in for his own stop a couple of laps later, while Mansell set about catching the McLarens, reeling off a series of Fastest Laps. Rosberg was next to pit for tyres, rejoining [![Image 5: FRA Patrese](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-patrese.jpg?w=300&h=204)](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-patrese.jpg)fourth, which promoted Mansell to second and Piquet to third, but Prost continued racing, even after a big lock-up under braking on lap 31 which must have flat-spotted his already old tyres. With a 12-second lead over Mansell decreasing all the time, he surely couldn’t leave it much longer if he was to retain his lead. Eventually he did, rejoining second, some 16 seconds behind Mansell with Piquet rapidly gaining and Rosberg behind the Williams.

As Prost made his way through traffic, he was balked by Alboreto, himself trying to better his position as he diced with Tambay. Prost made his way through but as Piquet did so, Rosberg pulled off a daring move around the outside and took third place. The Brazilian’s car began dropping back almost immediately with electrical gremlins while Rosberg nearly wiped off a front wheel trying a similarly ambitious move to lap Patrese’s Brabham. Phillippe Streiff’s Tyrrell pulled off in flames on lap 43 – the French driver hopped out with no apparent ill effects, but the fire resisted all attempts by the marshals to snuff it out with hand extinguishers and a fire engine had to come and hose it down.

Mansell continued serenely on in the lead, until he came in for his second tyre stop on lap 50 which dropped him to second, emerging just in front of Rosberg’s McLaren. On fresh rubber, he quickly pulled away from his 1985 team-mate but the question was whether the new tyres would make him fast enough to catch and pass the one-stopping Prost before the end of the race. He started well, tearing chunks out of Prost’s lead over the next laps, and putting up a new fastest lap some two seconds faster than the previous one. By lap 57 he was right behind Prost and as they came round to begin lap 58, Mansell breezed past on at the first corner. Prost managed to stick with Mansell as the pair carved through traffic, but once out on [![Image 6: FRA Finish](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-finish.jpg?w=604)](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-finish.jpg)clear track, the Williams quickly pulled away.

And that was more or less how it finished; during the closing stages of the race, Piquet had an improvement in pace and reeled in Rosberg, making his way past the Finn just a few laps from the chequered flag. So Mansell took the win, with Prost second, Piquet third and Rosberg fourth, and the Ligiers of Arnoux and Laffite coming in fifth and sixth to round out the points.

[![Image 7: FRA Podium Mansell](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-podium-mansell.jpg?w=194&h=300)](https://f1since81.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/fra-podium-mansell.jpg)Mansell’s win put him second in the title race, just a point behind Prost; both overtaking the unfortunate Senna. In the constructors’ stakes, Williams extended their lead over McLaren thanks to Piquet’s heroics in the closing stages.

The **1986 French Grand Prix**, otherwise known as the **[72 e Grand Prix de France](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/French_Grand_Prix "French Grand Prix")**, was the eighth round of the [1986](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_Formula_One_Season "1986 Formula One Season")[FIA](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/FIA "FIA")[Formula One World Championship](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One"), staged at the [Circuit Paul Ricard](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Circuit_Paul_Ricard "Circuit Paul Ricard") on the [6 July](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/July_6 "July 6") 1986.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) The race, which marked the halfway point in the 1986 campaign, would see [Nigel Mansell](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Nigel_Mansell "Nigel Mansell") claim [victory](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Victory "Victory") as [Alain Prost](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost") moved to the top of the Championship.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

The switch to the shorter circuit at Paul Ricard had been enforced after [Elio de Angelis'](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Elio_de_Angelis "Elio de Angelis") fatal accident at the circuit a month earlier.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) Indeed, the new circuit completely cut off the Esses where the Italian had flown off the circuit in the [Brabham](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Brabham "Brabham")-[BMW](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/BMW "BMW"), and greatly reduced the length of the Mistral straight.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

It was Championship leader, and de Angelis' former teammate [Ayrton Senna](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna") who claimed [pole](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Pole "Pole") position during [qualifying](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Qualifying "Qualifying"), the Brazilian lapping the shortened circuit in 1:06.526.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)[Nigel Mansell](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Nigel_Mansell "Nigel Mansell") would, as ever, claim second for [Williams](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Williams_F1 "Williams F1")-[Honda](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Honda "Honda") ahead of his teammate [Nelson Piquet](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet"), while Prost would start from fifth behind [René Arnoux](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Ren%C3%A9_Arnoux "René Arnoux").[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

The start of the race would see Mansell sprint ahead of Senna, while Arnoux, [Gerhard Berger](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Gerhard_Berger "Gerhard Berger"), Prost and [Johnny Dumfries](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Johnny_Dumfries "Johnny Dumfries") all getting the jump on Piquet.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) The Brazilian was hence left to fend off [Keke Rosberg](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Keke_Rosberg "Keke Rosberg") as he tried to hang onto seventh, while [Michele Alboreto](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Michele_Alboreto "Michele Alboreto") was left stranded on the grid after stalling.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

The early stages would see Mansell establish a small lead at the head of the field, while Senna spectacularly crashed out of contention when he hit an oil slick left by [Andrea de Cesaris](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Andrea_de_Cesaris "Andrea de Cesaris").[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) That put Arnoux up into second ahead of Berger, although the Austrian racer was coming under constant attack from the two [McLaren](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/McLaren_Racing "McLaren Racing")-[TAG](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Techniques_d%27Avant_Garde "Techniques d'Avant Garde")[Porsches](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Porsche "Porsche") as the early laps ticked away.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

Ultimately Berger's resistance would be broken before the end of lap ten, before the Austrian ultimately removed himself from the proceedings by slamming into the back of [Christian Danner](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Christian_Danner "Christian Danner").[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) Prost and Rosberg, meanwhile, would be left to attack Arnoux for second, and would duly complete their respective moves on the [Ligier](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Equipe_Ligier "Equipe Ligier")-[Renault](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Renault_F1 "Renault F1") before the end of the eighteenth lap.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

Mansell would pit from the lead a few laps later, the Brit opting for a two stop strategy rather than the McLarens' one.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) As such Mansell would drop behind both Prost and Rosberg mid-race, although after his second stop the Brit would be able to retake the lead with ease with fresher rubber.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

Indeed, barring a late move by Piquet on Rosberg the race would effectively be over by the end of lap 58.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) Mansell therefore claimed victory at a canter from Prost and Piquet, while Rosberg was frustrated to slip to fourth in the closing stages as his tyres faded badly.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) The remaining points would go to the two Ligiers, with Arnoux ahead of [Jacques Laffite](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Jacques_Laffite "Jacques Laffite").[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

The results of the race meant that Prost re-took the lead in the Championship at the halfway mark, a point ahead of Mansell in second while Senna dropped three behind in third. In the Constructors Championship, meanwhile, it was Williams-Honda who ended the afternoon on top, five ahead of McLaren-TAG Porsche.

Victory in Detroit had propelled [Ayrton Senna](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna") back into the lead of the Championship, with the Brazilian having opened out a three point lead over [Alain Prost](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost"). Furthermore, with [Nigel Mansell](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Nigel_Mansell "Nigel Mansell") just four points further back in third, it seemed as if it would be a three way fight for the Championship, with all three drivers holding two wins across the first seven races. Behind, [Nelson Piquet](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") was ten points off his third placed teammate, with [Keke Rosberg](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Keke_Rosberg "Keke Rosberg") even further back in fifth.

It was a similar picture the Constructors Championship at the start of the French Grand Prix weekend, with [Williams](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Williams_F1 "Williams F1")-[Honda](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Honda "Honda") and [McLaren](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/McLaren_Racing "McLaren Racing")-[TAG](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Techniques_d%27Avant_Garde "Techniques d'Avant Garde")[Porsche](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Porsche "Porsche") having ended the Detroit weekend just a point apart. It was the Anglo-Japanese combination, rather than the Anglo-German alliance that led, before an eleven point gap back to third placed [Lotus](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Team_Lotus "Team Lotus")-[Renault](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Renault_F1 "Renault F1"). Indeed, the Ethel based squad were also in the hunt for the crown, provided that second driver [Johnny Dumfries](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Johnny_Dumfries "Johnny Dumfries") became a regular scorer, having left [Ligier](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Equipe_Ligier "Equipe Ligier")-[Renault](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Renault_F1 "Renault F1") in an increasingly distant fourth.

The **1986 French Grand Prix**, otherwise known as the **[72 e Grand Prix de France](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/French_Grand_Prix "French Grand Prix")**, was the eighth round of the [1986](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_Formula_One_Season "1986 Formula One Season")[FIA](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/FIA "FIA")[Formula One World Championship](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One"), staged at the [Circuit Paul Ricard](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Circuit_Paul_Ricard "Circuit Paul Ricard") on the [6 July](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/July_6 "July 6") 1986.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) The race, which marked the halfway point in the 1986 campaign, would see [Nigel Mansell](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Nigel_Mansell "Nigel Mansell") claim [victory](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Victory "Victory") as [Alain Prost](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost") moved to the top of the Championship.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

The switch to the shorter circuit at Paul Ricard had been enforced after [Elio de Angelis'](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Elio_de_Angelis "Elio de Angelis") fatal accident at the circuit a month earlier.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) Indeed, the new circuit completely cut off the Esses where the Italian had flown off the circuit in the [Brabham](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Brabham "Brabham")-[BMW](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/BMW "BMW"), and greatly reduced the length of the Mistral straight.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

It was Championship leader, and de Angelis' former teammate [Ayrton Senna](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna") who claimed [pole](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Pole "Pole") position during [qualifying](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Qualifying "Qualifying"), the Brazilian lapping the shortened circuit in 1:06.526.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)[Nigel Mansell](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Nigel_Mansell "Nigel Mansell") would, as ever, claim second for [Williams](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Williams_F1 "Williams F1")-[Honda](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Honda "Honda") ahead of his teammate [Nelson Piquet](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet"), while Prost would start from fifth behind [René Arnoux](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Ren%C3%A9_Arnoux "René Arnoux").[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

The start of the race would see Mansell sprint ahead of Senna, while Arnoux, [Gerhard Berger](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Gerhard_Berger "Gerhard Berger"), Prost and [Johnny Dumfries](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Johnny_Dumfries "Johnny Dumfries") all getting the jump on Piquet.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) The Brazilian was hence left to fend off [Keke Rosberg](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Keke_Rosberg "Keke Rosberg") as he tried to hang onto seventh, while [Michele Alboreto](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Michele_Alboreto "Michele Alboreto") was left stranded on the grid after stalling.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

The early stages would see Mansell establish a small lead at the head of the field, while Senna spectacularly crashed out of contention when he hit an oil slick left by [Andrea de Cesaris](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Andrea_de_Cesaris "Andrea de Cesaris").[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) That put Arnoux up into second ahead of Berger, although the Austrian racer was coming under constant attack from the two [McLaren](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/McLaren_Racing "McLaren Racing")-[TAG](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Techniques_d%27Avant_Garde "Techniques d'Avant Garde")[Porsches](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Porsche "Porsche") as the early laps ticked away.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

Ultimately Berger's resistance would be broken before the end of lap ten, before the Austrian ultimately removed himself from the proceedings by slamming into the back of [Christian Danner](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Christian_Danner "Christian Danner").[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) Prost and Rosberg, meanwhile, would be left to attack Arnoux for second, and would duly complete their respective moves on the [Ligier](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Equipe_Ligier "Equipe Ligier")-[Renault](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Renault_F1 "Renault F1") before the end of the eighteenth lap.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

Mansell would pit from the lead a few laps later, the Brit opting for a two stop strategy rather than the McLarens' one.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) As such Mansell would drop behind both Prost and Rosberg mid-race, although after his second stop the Brit would be able to retake the lead with ease with fresher rubber.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

Indeed, barring a late move by Piquet on Rosberg the race would effectively be over by the end of lap 58.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) Mansell therefore claimed victory at a canter from Prost and Piquet, while Rosberg was frustrated to slip to fourth in the closing stages as his tyres faded badly.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) The remaining points would go to the two Ligiers, with Arnoux ahead of [Jacques Laffite](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Jacques_Laffite "Jacques Laffite").[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

The results of the race meant that Prost re-took the lead in the Championship at the halfway mark, a point ahead of Mansell in second while Senna dropped three behind in third. In the Constructors Championship, meanwhile, it was Williams-Honda who ended the afternoon on top, five ahead of McLaren-TAG Porsche.

Victory in Detroit had propelled [Ayrton Senna](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna") back into the lead of the Championship, with the Brazilian having opened out a three point lead over [Alain Prost](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost"). Furthermore, with [Nigel Mansell](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Nigel_Mansell "Nigel Mansell") just four points further back in third, it seemed as if it would be a three way fight for the Championship, with all three drivers holding two wins across the first seven races. Behind, [Nelson Piquet](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") was ten points off his third placed teammate, with [Keke Rosberg](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Keke_Rosberg "Keke Rosberg") even further back in fifth.

It was a similar picture the Constructors Championship at the start of the French Grand Prix weekend, with [Williams](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Williams_F1 "Williams F1")-[Honda](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Honda "Honda") and [McLaren](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/McLaren_Racing "McLaren Racing")-[TAG](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Techniques_d%27Avant_Garde "Techniques d'Avant Garde")[Porsche](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Porsche "Porsche") having ended the Detroit weekend just a point apart. It was the Anglo-Japanese combination, rather than the Anglo-German alliance that led, before an eleven point gap back to third placed [Lotus](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Team_Lotus "Team Lotus")-[Renault](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Renault_F1 "Renault F1"). Indeed, the Ethel based squad were also in the hunt for the crown, provided that second driver [Johnny Dumfries](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Johnny_Dumfries "Johnny Dumfries") became a regular scorer, having left [Ligier](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Equipe_Ligier "Equipe Ligier")-[Renault](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Renault_F1 "Renault F1") in an increasingly distant fourth.

[Nigel Mansell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Mansell "Nigel Mansell"), driving for [Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_Grand_Prix_Engineering "Williams Grand Prix Engineering"), finished runner-up to Prost by two points after dramatically retiring from the final race.

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/Nelson_Piquet_at_the_West_German_Formula_One_Grand_Prix_in_Hockenheim_in_1987_%28JOKAMAA2F-7%29.tif/lossy-page1-250px-Nelson_Piquet_at_the_West_German_Formula_One_Grand_Prix_in_Hockenheim_in_1987_%28JOKAMAA2F-7%29.tif.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nelson_Piquet_at_the_West_German_Formula_One_Grand_Prix_in_Hockenheim_in_1987_(JOKAMAA2F-7).tif)

Mansell's Williams teammate and then two-time champion [Nelson Piquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") (pictured in 1987) finished third, three points behind Prost.

[Lotus-Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Lotus "Team Lotus") finished third in the Constructors' Championship with the [Lotus 98T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotus_98T "Lotus 98T").

The **1986 FIA Formula One World Championship** was the 40th season of [FIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A9d%C3%A9ration_Internationale_de_l'Automobile "Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile")[Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One") motor racing. It featured the 1986 Formula One World Championship for Drivers and the 1986 Formula One World Championship for Manufacturers, both of which commenced on 23 March and ended on 26 October after sixteen races. The Drivers' Championship was won by [Alain Prost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-FIA_P86-1) Prost was the first driver to win back-to-back Drivers' Championships since [Jack Brabham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Brabham "Jack Brabham") in 1959 and 1960. Together with Prost, [Nigel Mansell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Mansell "Nigel Mansell"), [Nelson Piquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") and [Ayrton Senna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna") dominated throughout the season and formed what was dubbed as the "Gang of Four".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-Goodwood-3) The 1986 season also marked the final Formula One season of [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Formula_One_World_Championship "1982 Formula One World Championship") Drivers' Champion [Keke Rosberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keke_Rosberg "Keke Rosberg") who retired from the sport at the end of season following a difficult season with [McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren "McLaren").

After 1986, [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_F1 "Renault F1") left the sport as an engine supplier due to [company restructuring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault#Restructuring_(1981%E2%80%931995) "Renault"), only to return in [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_Formula_One_World_Championship "1989 Formula One World Championship"). The Constructors' Championship was won by [Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_Grand_Prix_Engineering "Williams Grand Prix Engineering")-[Honda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_in_Formula_One "Honda in Formula One"). Honda became the first [Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan") engine supplier to win a Constructors' Championship.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-FIA_P87-4)

### Team changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1986_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Team changes")]

[![Image 60](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Gerhard_Berger_1986_Detroit.jpg/250px-Gerhard_Berger_1986_Detroit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gerhard_Berger_1986_Detroit.jpg)

[Benetton Formula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benetton_Formula "Benetton Formula") made their entrance in F1.

*   Two factory-backed constructors left Formula One after the [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Formula_One_World_Championship "1985 Formula One World Championship") season: [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_in_Formula_One "Renault in Formula One") (only staying one more year as an engine supplier) and [Alfa Romeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfa_Romeo_in_Formula_One "Alfa Romeo in Formula One"). Two other teams had already folded during the season: [RAM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAM_Racing "RAM Racing") and [Spirit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirit_Racing "Spirit Racing").
*   The [Toleman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toleman "Toleman") team was bought by the [Benetton Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benetton_Group "Benetton Group") and renamed [Benetton Formula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benetton_Formula "Benetton Formula").
*   Shortly before the season began, [Frank Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Williams_(Formula_One) "Frank Williams (Formula One)") was involved in a road accident in [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France") that left him in a [wheelchair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheelchair "Wheelchair"). Technical director and part-owner [Patrick Head](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Head "Patrick Head") would be forced to run the team in all departments, in addition to his design and engineering work.

#### Mid-season changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1986_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Mid-season changes")]

*   When entering the sport in 1985, [Haas Lola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haas_Lola "Haas Lola") encountered delays in the development of their first car, and the specially developed [Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Motor_Company "Ford Motor Company")-[Cosworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosworth "Cosworth")[V6 turbo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosworth#The_GBA_V6 "Cosworth") was not ready either. So their first chassis was adjusted to be powered by a four-[cylinder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cylinder_(engine) "Cylinder (engine)")[Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hart_Racing_Engines "Hart Racing Engines")[turbo engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turbocharger "Turbocharger") and could only make its debut in September. It was not until the third race of 1986 that the team could get delivery of the Cosworth engine and switch to their second car, specifically designed around it.
*   The small [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France") constructor [AGS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automobiles_Gonfaronnaises_Sportives "Automobiles Gonfaronnaises Sportives") made their debut in the [Italian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Italian_Grand_Prix "1986 Italian Grand Prix"). Their track record from [F2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_Two "Formula Two") and [F3000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Formula_3000 "International Formula 3000") was not particularly promising and the team had no more than seven employees. Their first F1 car existed of as many [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_in_Formula_One "Renault in Formula One") parts as was legal, bolted onto an F3000 chassis. It was powered by a well-used [Motori Moderni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motori_Moderni "Motori Moderni") engine and driven by [Ivan Capelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Capelli "Ivan Capelli"), while he was still on his way to become [International F3000 champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_International_Formula_3000_Championship "1986 International Formula 3000 Championship").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-5)

### Driver changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1986_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Driver changes")]

*   After triple world champion [Niki Lauda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niki_Lauda "Niki Lauda") retired, [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Formula_One_World_Championship "1982 Formula One World Championship") champion [Keke Rosberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keke_Rosberg "Keke Rosberg") took his place at [McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren "McLaren"). [Nelson Piquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet"), two world championships under his belt, took the opportunity to leave [Brabham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brabham "Brabham") after seven seasons, and move to [Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_Grand_Prix_Engineering "Williams Grand Prix Engineering").
*   [Elio de Angelis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elio_de_Angelis "Elio de Angelis") had chosen to leave [Lotus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Lotus "Team Lotus"), frustrated that the team's efforts were being focused mostly on [Ayrton Senna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna"). He was granted Piquet's seat at Brabham. [Derek Warwick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Warwick "Derek Warwick") was originally signed to replace the [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy"), but Senna gave his preference to [Johnny Dumfries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Dumfries "Johnny Dumfries"), [British F3 champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_British_Formula_Three_Championship "1984 British Formula Three Championship") and [European F3 runner-up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_FIA_European_Formula_3_Championship "1984 FIA European Formula 3 Championship") in 1984.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-6)
*   A lot of other driver changes happened in the lower-ranking teams.

#### Mid-season changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1986_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Mid-season changes")]

*   [Derek Warwick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Warwick "Derek Warwick") was left without a drive after the deal with [Lotus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Lotus "Team Lotus") fell through. He ended up at Brabham in May 1986, after De Angelis died following a fiery crash during private testing at [Circuit Paul Ricard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_Paul_Ricard "Circuit Paul Ricard").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-7)
*   In [warm-up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_racing#Race_start "Formula One racing") to the [Canadian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Canadian_Grand_Prix "1986 Canadian Grand Prix"), [Patrick Tambay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Tambay "Patrick Tambay"), driving for [Haas Lola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haas_Lola "Haas Lola"), suffered [suspension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suspension_(mechanics) "Suspension (mechanics)") failure and a huge accident injured both his feet.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-8) Team owner [Carl Haas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Haas "Carl Haas") tried to get [1978](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_Formula_One_season "1978 Formula One season") world champion [Mario Andretti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti "Mario Andretti") as a replacement, but he declined and recommended his son [Michael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Andretti "Michael Andretti"). When Michael was unable to obtain a [FIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIA "FIA")[Superlicence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superlicence "Superlicence"), however, Haas turned to the experienced [Eddie Cheever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Cheever "Eddie Cheever"). Tambay returned for [French Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix "1986 French Grand Prix").
*   After fives races of the F1 season, [Marc Surer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Surer "Marc Surer") suffered a serious accident when competing in the 1986 ADAC Hessen-Rallye. [Christian Danner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Danner "Christian Danner") moved to [Arrows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrows_Grand_Prix_International "Arrows Grand Prix International") to replace him. Danner's seat at [Osella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osella "Osella") was filled by [Allen Berg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Berg "Allen Berg"). It was the [Canadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada")'s debut, after talks with Arrows, [Tyrrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrrell_Racing "Tyrrell Racing"), [RAM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAM_Racing "RAM Racing") and [Spirit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirit_Racing "Spirit Racing") had not come to fruition. When his sponsorship money ran out, he was replaced at the [Italian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Italian_Grand_Prix "1986 Italian Grand Prix") by [Alex Caffi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Caffi "Alex Caffi"), granting him a debut at his home race, but further sponsorship did mean that Berg was able to see out the season.
*   At the start of the [British Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_British_Grand_Prix "1986 British Grand Prix"), [Jacques Laffite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Laffite "Jacques Laffite") was involved in a multi-car pile-up. He broke both legs and it ended his F1 career. [Philippe Alliot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippe_Alliot "Philippe Alliot") returned to take his seat at [Ligier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equipe_Ligier "Equipe Ligier"), after driving two seasons for [RAM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAM_Racing "RAM Racing").

### Calendar changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1986_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Calendar changes")]

*   The [Spanish Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Grand_Prix "Spanish Grand Prix") returned to the calendar for the first time in five years and was held at the newly built [Circuito de Jerez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuito_de_Jerez "Circuito de Jerez"). (In [1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Formula_One_World_Championship "1984 Formula One World Championship") and [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Formula_One_World_Championship "1985 Formula One World Championship"), Formula One had tried to stage the race in [Fuengirola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuengirola "Fuengirola").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-DH-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-11)) The owners of the [Jarama circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuito_del_Jarama "Circuito del Jarama") tried to get the slot of the [European Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Grand_Prix "European Grand Prix"), but were unsuccessful.
*   The [Belgian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Grand_Prix "Belgian Grand Prix") was moved up to May to avoid the chance of hot and dry weather, after the asphalt broke up in practice for the 1985 edition under the immense power of the cars.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-DH-9)
*   The [British Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Grand_Prix "British Grand Prix") was moved from [Silverstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silverstone_Circuit "Silverstone Circuit") to [Brands Hatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brands_Hatch "Brands Hatch"), in keeping with the event-sharing arrangement between the two circuits. The [1986 British Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_British_Grand_Prix "1986 British Grand Prix") would be the last at [Brands Hatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brands_Hatch "Brands Hatch"), as from [1987](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_Formula_One_World_Championship "1987 Formula One World Championship"), it would be permanently held at Silverstone (under [FISA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A9d%C3%A9ration_Internationale_du_Sport_Automobile "Fédération Internationale du Sport Automobile")'s "one country, one circuit" rule[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-RaceFans-12)).
*   The [German Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Grand_Prix "German Grand Prix") returned to the [Hockenheimring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hockenheimring "Hockenheimring") after using the [Nürburgring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N%C3%BCrburgring "Nürburgring") for 1985, and would be permanently held at Hockenheim (again, "one country, one circuit"[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-RaceFans-12)).
*   The [Hungarian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_Grand_Prix "Hungarian Grand Prix") was organised for the first time. It was the first F1 race to take place behind the [Iron Curtain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Curtain "Iron Curtain").
*   The [Portuguese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Grand_Prix "Portuguese Grand Prix") was moved back to September.
*   The [Mexican Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Grand_Prix "Mexican Grand Prix") returned for the first time since [1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_Formula_One_season "1970 Formula One season"). The [Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aut%C3%B3dromo_Hermanos_Rodr%C3%ADguez "Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez") in [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City") was upgraded to a new layout to improve safety. (The race was originally supposed to return in 1985 but was cancelled due to the [1985 Mexico City earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Mexico_City_earthquake "1985 Mexico City earthquake").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-13))

## Regulation changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1986_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Regulation changes")]

### Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1986_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Background")]

Back in [1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Formula_One_season "1980 Formula One season"), [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_in_Formula_One "Renault in Formula One") proved that [turbocharged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turbocharger "Turbocharger") engines were the way to success and by the half-way point in the [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Formula_One_World_Championship "1985 Formula One World Championship") season, all teams had followed their example. The [FIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIA "FIA") saw that the power output from turbo engines had doubled in the past six years. The 1986 F1 cars in qualifying trim proved to be the most powerful Grand Prix cars in history. Manufacturers mentioned numbers above 1,400 bhp (1,000 kW), powering cars that weighed just 540 kg (1,190 lb) giving a staggering power-to-weight ratio of 2,500 hp/ton.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-Goodwood-3) This [power output](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsepower "Horsepower") was only seen in [qualifying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_racing#Qualifying "Formula One racing") trim, since the specially prepared engines, [tyres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_tyres "Formula One tyres") and [gearboxes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gearbox "Gearbox") could only hold on for two to four laps under this immense force before destroying themselves,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-16) and in race trim, with the engines limited in power to conserve them to run a 190-mile (306 km) race distance, the cars were not much slower.

So after mandating turbocharged engines for 1986, the governing body decided to re-allow [naturally aspirated engines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naturally_aspirated_engines "Naturally aspirated engines") for [1987](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_Formula_One_World_Championship "1987 Formula One World Championship"), and at the same time started reining in the power of turbo engines, before banning them altogether for the [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_Formula_One_World_Championship "1989 Formula One World Championship") season.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-18)

### Technical regulations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1986_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Technical regulations")]

*   1.5 [litre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Litre "Litre")[turbocharged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turbocharger "Turbocharger") engines compulsory (with unlimited number of [cylinders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cylinder_(engine) "Cylinder (engine)"), [RPM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutions_per_minute "Revolutions per minute") and [power output](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsepower "Horsepower")).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-F1technical-20)
*   Fuel use during the race was limited from 220 L (58 US gal) to 195 L (52 US gal). This led to fuel saving playing a major role in team strategy during the season.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-F1technical-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-21)

### Event regulations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1986_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Event regulations")]

*   Catch-fencing was banned.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-F1technical-20)
*   After the accident and death of [Elio de Angelis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elio_de_Angelis "Elio de Angelis") in testing, a permanent team of professional firefighters, [FIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIA "FIA") medical service inspector and medevac [helicopter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helicopter "Helicopter") were made mandatory at all testing and race events.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-F1technical-20)

[Alain Prost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost") (pictured in 1985) won his second consecutive Drivers' Championship, driving for [McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren "McLaren"). The first driver in 26 years to win consecutive titles.

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/Nigelcropped.jpg/250px-Nigelcropped.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nigelcropped.jpg)

[Nigel Mansell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Mansell "Nigel Mansell"), driving for [Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_Grand_Prix_Engineering "Williams Grand Prix Engineering"), finished runner-up to Prost by two points after dramatically retiring from the final race.

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/Nelson_Piquet_at_the_West_German_Formula_One_Grand_Prix_in_Hockenheim_in_1987_%28JOKAMAA2F-7%29.tif/lossy-page1-250px-Nelson_Piquet_at_the_West_German_Formula_One_Grand_Prix_in_Hockenheim_in_1987_%28JOKAMAA2F-7%29.tif.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nelson_Piquet_at_the_West_German_Formula_One_Grand_Prix_in_Hockenheim_in_1987_(JOKAMAA2F-7).tif)

Mansell's Williams teammate and then two-time champion [Nelson Piquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") (pictured in 1987) finished third, three points behind Prost.

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/Williams_FW11_Honda_Collection_Hall.jpg/250px-Williams_FW11_Honda_Collection_Hall.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Williams_FW11_Honda_Collection_Hall.jpg)

[Williams-Honda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams-Honda "Williams-Honda") won the [World Constructors' Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Constructors'_Championship "World Constructors' Championship") with the [Williams FW11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_FW11 "Williams FW11").

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Stuttgart_Jul_2012_31_%28Porsche_Museum_-_1986_McLaren_TAG_MP_4-2_C_Formel_1%29.JPG/250px-Stuttgart_Jul_2012_31_%28Porsche_Museum_-_1986_McLaren_TAG_MP_4-2_C_Formel_1%29.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Stuttgart_Jul_2012_31_(Porsche_Museum_-_1986_McLaren_TAG_MP_4-2_C_Formel_1).JPG)

[McLaren-TAG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mclaren "Mclaren") finished runner-up in the Constructors' Championship with the [McLaren MP4/2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_MP4/2 "McLaren MP4/2").

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/65/Senna_Brands_1986.jpg/250px-Senna_Brands_1986.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Senna_Brands_1986.jpg)

[Lotus-Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Lotus "Team Lotus") finished third in the Constructors' Championship with the [Lotus 98T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotus_98T "Lotus 98T").

The **1986 FIA Formula One World Championship** was the 40th season of [FIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A9d%C3%A9ration_Internationale_de_l'Automobile "Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile")[Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One") motor racing. It featured the 1986 Formula One World Championship for Drivers and the 1986 Formula One World Championship for Manufacturers, both of which commenced on 23 March and ended on 26 October after sixteen races. The Drivers' Championship was won by [Alain Prost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-FIA_P86-1) Prost was the first driver to win back-to-back Drivers' Championships since [Jack Brabham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Brabham "Jack Brabham") in 1959 and 1960. Together with Prost, [Nigel Mansell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Mansell "Nigel Mansell"), [Nelson Piquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") and [Ayrton Senna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna") dominated throughout the season and formed what was dubbed as the "Gang of Four".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-Goodwood-3) The 1986 season also marked the final Formula One season of [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Formula_One_World_Championship "1982 Formula One World Championship") Drivers' Champion [Keke Rosberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keke_Rosberg "Keke Rosberg") who retired from the sport at the end of season following a difficult season with [McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren "McLaren").

After 1986, [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_F1 "Renault F1") left the sport as an engine supplier due to [company restructuring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault#Restructuring_(1981%E2%80%931995) "Renault"), only to return in [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_Formula_One_World_Championship "1989 Formula One World Championship"). The Constructors' Championship was won by [Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_Grand_Prix_Engineering "Williams Grand Prix Engineering")-[Honda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_in_Formula_One "Honda in Formula One"). Honda became the first [Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan") engine supplier to win a Constructors' Championship.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-FIA_P87-4)
