### Team changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1986_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Team changes")]

[![Image 60](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Gerhard_Berger_1986_Detroit.jpg/250px-Gerhard_Berger_1986_Detroit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gerhard_Berger_1986_Detroit.jpg)

[Benetton Formula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benetton_Formula "Benetton Formula") made their entrance in F1.

*   Two factory-backed constructors left Formula One after the [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Formula_One_World_Championship "1985 Formula One World Championship") season: [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_in_Formula_One "Renault in Formula One") (only staying one more year as an engine supplier) and [Alfa Romeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfa_Romeo_in_Formula_One "Alfa Romeo in Formula One"). Two other teams had already folded during the season: [RAM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAM_Racing "RAM Racing") and [Spirit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirit_Racing "Spirit Racing").
*   The [Toleman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toleman "Toleman") team was bought by the [Benetton Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benetton_Group "Benetton Group") and renamed [Benetton Formula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benetton_Formula "Benetton Formula").
*   Shortly before the season began, [Frank Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Williams_(Formula_One) "Frank Williams (Formula One)") was involved in a road accident in [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France") that left him in a [wheelchair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheelchair "Wheelchair"). Technical director and part-owner [Patrick Head](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Head "Patrick Head") would be forced to run the team in all departments, in addition to his design and engineering work.

#### Mid-season changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1986_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Mid-season changes")]

*   When entering the sport in 1985, [Haas Lola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haas_Lola "Haas Lola") encountered delays in the development of their first car, and the specially developed [Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Motor_Company "Ford Motor Company")-[Cosworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosworth "Cosworth")[V6 turbo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosworth#The_GBA_V6 "Cosworth") was not ready either. So their first chassis was adjusted to be powered by a four-[cylinder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cylinder_(engine) "Cylinder (engine)")[Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hart_Racing_Engines "Hart Racing Engines")[turbo engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turbocharger "Turbocharger") and could only make its debut in September. It was not until the third race of 1986 that the team could get delivery of the Cosworth engine and switch to their second car, specifically designed around it.
*   The small [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France") constructor [AGS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automobiles_Gonfaronnaises_Sportives "Automobiles Gonfaronnaises Sportives") made their debut in the [Italian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Italian_Grand_Prix "1986 Italian Grand Prix"). Their track record from [F2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_Two "Formula Two") and [F3000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Formula_3000 "International Formula 3000") was not particularly promising and the team had no more than seven employees. Their first F1 car existed of as many [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_in_Formula_One "Renault in Formula One") parts as was legal, bolted onto an F3000 chassis. It was powered by a well-used [Motori Moderni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motori_Moderni "Motori Moderni") engine and driven by [Ivan Capelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Capelli "Ivan Capelli"), while he was still on his way to become [International F3000 champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_International_Formula_3000_Championship "1986 International Formula 3000 Championship").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-5)

### Driver changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1986_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Driver changes")]

*   After triple world champion [Niki Lauda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niki_Lauda "Niki Lauda") retired, [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Formula_One_World_Championship "1982 Formula One World Championship") champion [Keke Rosberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keke_Rosberg "Keke Rosberg") took his place at [McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren "McLaren"). [Nelson Piquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet"), two world championships under his belt, took the opportunity to leave [Brabham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brabham "Brabham") after seven seasons, and move to [Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_Grand_Prix_Engineering "Williams Grand Prix Engineering").
*   [Elio de Angelis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elio_de_Angelis "Elio de Angelis") had chosen to leave [Lotus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Lotus "Team Lotus"), frustrated that the team's efforts were being focused mostly on [Ayrton Senna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna"). He was granted Piquet's seat at Brabham. [Derek Warwick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Warwick "Derek Warwick") was originally signed to replace the [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy"), but Senna gave his preference to [Johnny Dumfries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Dumfries "Johnny Dumfries"), [British F3 champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_British_Formula_Three_Championship "1984 British Formula Three Championship") and [European F3 runner-up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_FIA_European_Formula_3_Championship "1984 FIA European Formula 3 Championship") in 1984.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-6)
*   A lot of other driver changes happened in the lower-ranking teams.

#### Mid-season changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1986_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Mid-season changes")]

*   [Derek Warwick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Warwick "Derek Warwick") was left without a drive after the deal with [Lotus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Lotus "Team Lotus") fell through. He ended up at Brabham in May 1986, after De Angelis died following a fiery crash during private testing at [Circuit Paul Ricard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_Paul_Ricard "Circuit Paul Ricard").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-7)
*   In [warm-up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_racing#Race_start "Formula One racing") to the [Canadian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Canadian_Grand_Prix "1986 Canadian Grand Prix"), [Patrick Tambay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Tambay "Patrick Tambay"), driving for [Haas Lola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haas_Lola "Haas Lola"), suffered [suspension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suspension_(mechanics) "Suspension (mechanics)") failure and a huge accident injured both his feet.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-8) Team owner [Carl Haas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Haas "Carl Haas") tried to get [1978](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_Formula_One_season "1978 Formula One season") world champion [Mario Andretti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Andretti "Mario Andretti") as a replacement, but he declined and recommended his son [Michael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Andretti "Michael Andretti"). When Michael was unable to obtain a [FIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIA "FIA")[Superlicence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superlicence "Superlicence"), however, Haas turned to the experienced [Eddie Cheever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Cheever "Eddie Cheever"). Tambay returned for [French Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_French_Grand_Prix "1986 French Grand Prix").
*   After fives races of the F1 season, [Marc Surer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Surer "Marc Surer") suffered a serious accident when competing in the 1986 ADAC Hessen-Rallye. [Christian Danner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Danner "Christian Danner") moved to [Arrows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrows_Grand_Prix_International "Arrows Grand Prix International") to replace him. Danner's seat at [Osella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osella "Osella") was filled by [Allen Berg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Berg "Allen Berg"). It was the [Canadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada")'s debut, after talks with Arrows, [Tyrrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrrell_Racing "Tyrrell Racing"), [RAM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAM_Racing "RAM Racing") and [Spirit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirit_Racing "Spirit Racing") had not come to fruition. When his sponsorship money ran out, he was replaced at the [Italian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Italian_Grand_Prix "1986 Italian Grand Prix") by [Alex Caffi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Caffi "Alex Caffi"), granting him a debut at his home race, but further sponsorship did mean that Berg was able to see out the season.
*   At the start of the [British Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_British_Grand_Prix "1986 British Grand Prix"), [Jacques Laffite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Laffite "Jacques Laffite") was involved in a multi-car pile-up. He broke both legs and it ended his F1 career. [Philippe Alliot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippe_Alliot "Philippe Alliot") returned to take his seat at [Ligier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equipe_Ligier "Equipe Ligier"), after driving two seasons for [RAM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAM_Racing "RAM Racing").

### Calendar changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1986_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Calendar changes")]

*   The [Spanish Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Grand_Prix "Spanish Grand Prix") returned to the calendar for the first time in five years and was held at the newly built [Circuito de Jerez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuito_de_Jerez "Circuito de Jerez"). (In [1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Formula_One_World_Championship "1984 Formula One World Championship") and [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Formula_One_World_Championship "1985 Formula One World Championship"), Formula One had tried to stage the race in [Fuengirola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuengirola "Fuengirola").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-DH-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-11)) The owners of the [Jarama circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuito_del_Jarama "Circuito del Jarama") tried to get the slot of the [European Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Grand_Prix "European Grand Prix"), but were unsuccessful.
*   The [Belgian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Grand_Prix "Belgian Grand Prix") was moved up to May to avoid the chance of hot and dry weather, after the asphalt broke up in practice for the 1985 edition under the immense power of the cars.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-DH-9)
*   The [British Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Grand_Prix "British Grand Prix") was moved from [Silverstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silverstone_Circuit "Silverstone Circuit") to [Brands Hatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brands_Hatch "Brands Hatch"), in keeping with the event-sharing arrangement between the two circuits. The [1986 British Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_British_Grand_Prix "1986 British Grand Prix") would be the last at [Brands Hatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brands_Hatch "Brands Hatch"), as from [1987](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_Formula_One_World_Championship "1987 Formula One World Championship"), it would be permanently held at Silverstone (under [FISA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A9d%C3%A9ration_Internationale_du_Sport_Automobile "Fédération Internationale du Sport Automobile")'s "one country, one circuit" rule[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-RaceFans-12)).
*   The [German Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Grand_Prix "German Grand Prix") returned to the [Hockenheimring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hockenheimring "Hockenheimring") after using the [Nürburgring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N%C3%BCrburgring "Nürburgring") for 1985, and would be permanently held at Hockenheim (again, "one country, one circuit"[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-RaceFans-12)).
*   The [Hungarian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_Grand_Prix "Hungarian Grand Prix") was organised for the first time. It was the first F1 race to take place behind the [Iron Curtain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Curtain "Iron Curtain").
*   The [Portuguese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Grand_Prix "Portuguese Grand Prix") was moved back to September.
*   The [Mexican Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Grand_Prix "Mexican Grand Prix") returned for the first time since [1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_Formula_One_season "1970 Formula One season"). The [Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aut%C3%B3dromo_Hermanos_Rodr%C3%ADguez "Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez") in [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City") was upgraded to a new layout to improve safety. (The race was originally supposed to return in 1985 but was cancelled due to the [1985 Mexico City earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Mexico_City_earthquake "1985 Mexico City earthquake").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-13))

### Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1986_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Background")]

Back in [1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Formula_One_season "1980 Formula One season"), [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_in_Formula_One "Renault in Formula One") proved that [turbocharged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turbocharger "Turbocharger") engines were the way to success and by the half-way point in the [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Formula_One_World_Championship "1985 Formula One World Championship") season, all teams had followed their example. The [FIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIA "FIA") saw that the power output from turbo engines had doubled in the past six years. The 1986 F1 cars in qualifying trim proved to be the most powerful Grand Prix cars in history. Manufacturers mentioned numbers above 1,400 bhp (1,000 kW), powering cars that weighed just 540 kg (1,190 lb) giving a staggering power-to-weight ratio of 2,500 hp/ton.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-Goodwood-3) This [power output](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsepower "Horsepower") was only seen in [qualifying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_racing#Qualifying "Formula One racing") trim, since the specially prepared engines, [tyres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_tyres "Formula One tyres") and [gearboxes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gearbox "Gearbox") could only hold on for two to four laps under this immense force before destroying themselves,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-16) and in race trim, with the engines limited in power to conserve them to run a 190-mile (306 km) race distance, the cars were not much slower.

So after mandating turbocharged engines for 1986, the governing body decided to re-allow [naturally aspirated engines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naturally_aspirated_engines "Naturally aspirated engines") for [1987](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_Formula_One_World_Championship "1987 Formula One World Championship"), and at the same time started reining in the power of turbo engines, before banning them altogether for the [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_Formula_One_World_Championship "1989 Formula One World Championship") season.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-18)

### Technical regulations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1986_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Technical regulations")]

*   1.5 [litre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Litre "Litre")[turbocharged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turbocharger "Turbocharger") engines compulsory (with unlimited number of [cylinders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cylinder_(engine) "Cylinder (engine)"), [RPM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutions_per_minute "Revolutions per minute") and [power output](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsepower "Horsepower")).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-F1technical-20)
*   Fuel use during the race was limited from 220 L (58 US gal) to 195 L (52 US gal). This led to fuel saving playing a major role in team strategy during the season.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-F1technical-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-21)

### Event regulations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1986_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Event regulations")]

*   Catch-fencing was banned.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-F1technical-20)
*   After the accident and death of [Elio de Angelis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elio_de_Angelis "Elio de Angelis") in testing, a permanent team of professional firefighters, [FIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIA "FIA") medical service inspector and medevac [helicopter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helicopter "Helicopter") were made mandatory at all testing and race events.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-F1technical-20)

Motor car race

The **1988 French Grand Prix** was a [Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One") motor race held on 3 July 1988 at the [Circuit Paul Ricard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_Paul_Ricard "Circuit Paul Ricard"), [Le Castellet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Castellet,_Var "Le Castellet, Var"). It was the seventh race of the [1988 Formula One World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Formula_One_World_Championship "1988 Formula One World Championship").

The 80-lap race was won by local driver [Alain Prost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost"), driving a [McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren "McLaren")-[Honda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_in_Formula_One "Honda in Formula One"), after he started from [pole position](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pole_position "Pole position"). Prost's Brazilian teammate [Ayrton Senna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna") finished second, with Italian [Michele Alboreto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Alboreto "Michele Alboreto") third in a [Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari").

## Qualifying

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1988_French_Grand_Prix&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Qualifying")]

The two [McLarens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_MP4/4 "McLaren MP4/4") lined up in their usual front row places, but, for the first time this season, [Alain Prost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost") was ahead of [Ayrton Senna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna"), the Frenchman beating the Brazilian by almost half a second to take his first pole since the [1986 Monaco Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Monaco_Grand_Prix "1986 Monaco Grand Prix") and in doing so stopping his teammate from a record-breaking 7th pole in succession. The two [Ferraris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrari_F1/87#F1/87/88C "Ferrari F1/87") filled the second row, [Gerhard Berger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerhard_Berger "Gerhard Berger") beating [Michele Alboreto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Alboreto "Michele Alboreto") by over 1.1 seconds, though neither driver believed they could race with the McLarens simply because of fuel consumption. On the third row were the two [normally-aspirated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naturally_aspirated_engine "Naturally aspirated engine")[Benettons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benetton_B188 "Benetton B188") of [Thierry Boutsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thierry_Boutsen "Thierry Boutsen") and [Alessandro Nannini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alessandro_Nannini "Alessandro Nannini"), while the [Lotuses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotus_100T "Lotus 100T") of [Nelson Piquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") and [Satoru Nakajima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satoru_Nakajima "Satoru Nakajima") filled the fourth row, Piquet being the last driver to qualify under 1:10. The top ten was completed by the [Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_FW12 "Williams FW12") of [Nigel Mansell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Mansell "Nigel Mansell") (over 2.7 seconds slower than Prost and almost 4 seconds slower than his [1987](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_French_Grand_Prix "1987 French Grand Prix") pole time) and the [March](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_881 "March 881") of [Ivan Capelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Capelli "Ivan Capelli"), who had recovered after fracturing his left foot in a crash during practice in [Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Detroit_Grand_Prix "1988 Detroit Grand Prix") two weeks before.

Meanwhile, [Ligier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equipe_Ligier "Equipe Ligier") had a disastrous weekend on their home turf with both [René Arnoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ren%C3%A9_Arnoux "René Arnoux"), a winner with [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_F1 "Renault F1") at the circuit in [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_French_Grand_Prix "1982 French Grand Prix"), and [Stefan Johansson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefan_Johansson "Stefan Johansson") failing to qualify, though they did have a celebration of sorts over the weekend as Arnoux turned 40 the day after the race. [Julian Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Bailey_(racing_driver) "Julian Bailey (racing driver)") also failed to qualify in his [Tyrrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrrell_017 "Tyrrell 017"), while [Piercarlo Ghinzani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piercarlo_Ghinzani "Piercarlo Ghinzani") qualified 22nd in his [Zakspeed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zakspeed_881 "Zakspeed 881") but was excluded for missing a weight check, thus promoting [Oscar Larrauri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Larrauri "Oscar Larrauri")'s [EuroBrun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EuroBrun_ER188 "EuroBrun ER188") to the last grid spot.

## Race summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1988_French_Grand_Prix&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Race summary")]

Prost led away from Senna and the two Ferraris, with Piquet passing the two Benettons for fifth. Despite worries in the McLaren pit about overly high fuel consumption (the fuel readouts in the cars were showing less fuel used than what the Honda telemetry was telling the team), Ron Dennis was reportedly prepared to let his drivers run out of fuel at the expense of a perfect season if it taught them to be more conservative given their obvious advantage over the field, though ultimately the onboard readouts were proved correct. Prost maintained a two-second advantage over Senna until the mid-race pit stops, while an early stop by Berger on lap 22 allowed teammate Alboreto through into third. While both McLarens were racing each other out front, they were still pulling away from the field at sometimes a second per lap.

Senna made his pit stop three laps before Prost, enabling him to take the lead thanks to a slow stop for Prost with a sticking front wheel, but traffic on the Mistral Straight (including a less than helpful Piquet who most likely enjoyed seeing Senna lose the lead to Prost at close quarters) and a gearbox problem allowed Prost to close right up to him and then overtake him on lap 61 as they lapped [Alex Caffi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Caffi "Alex Caffi") and [Pierluigi Martini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierluigi_Martini "Pierluigi Martini") at the Signes corner. Meanwhile, Berger reclaimed third only for Alboreto to pass him again during the pit stops, while Mansell suffered his seventh consecutive retirement, dropping out on lap 49 with suspension problems, though he had been dropping back for a number of laps with power loss from his [Judd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judd_(engine)#CV "Judd (engine)")[V8 engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V8_engine "V8 engine"). After returning to the pits and getting himself cleaned up, the Englishman left the circuit profoundly fed up with the performance of the Williams, fuelling ongoing speculation in the press that he would leave the team at the end of the year to join Ferrari after the Italian team had announced they would not be keeping Alboreto for 1989. Despite the rumours turning out to be correct, Mansell continued to deny he was joining Ferrari.

In the closing laps, Prost pulled away as Senna's gearbox troubles continued, losing several gears. The Brazilian eventually finished nearly 32 seconds behind the Frenchman, though he was still nearly 35 seconds ahead of Alboreto, the last man on the lead lap. Berger was fourth ahead of Piquet, who also suffered gearbox problems in the later stages of the race; the final point went to the Benetton of Nannini. France was the first time since the [1987 Monaco Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_Monaco_Grand_Prix "1987 Monaco Grand Prix") that Alboreto had finished in front of his teammate in a race where they both finished. During the race Alboreto had the advantage of an almost perfectly balanced car, while Berger complained of severe understeer, something not needed at the high speed Signes corner at the end of the Mistral.

The fastest lap of the race, a 1:11.737 set by Prost on lap 45, was over two seconds slower than the 1:09.548 set by Piquet in a Honda-powered Williams the [previous year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_French_Grand_Prix "1987 French Grand Prix") – a consequence of the restrictions imposed on [turbocharged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turbocharger "Turbocharger") engines this season with the major difference being the speeds attained on the now 1 km long Mistral Straight. In 1987 the fastest turbo cars (Honda powered) were timed at 325 km/h (202 mph) on the straight. In 1988 the top speed was recorded at 311 km/h (193 mph).

For Prost it was his third win in his home Grand Prix after winning in both [1981](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_French_Grand_Prix "1981 French Grand Prix") at [Dijon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dijon-Prenois "Dijon-Prenois") (his first Grand Prix victory) and [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_French_Grand_Prix "1983 French Grand Prix") at the full length Paul Ricard. On both occasions he had been driving for the factory [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equipe_Renault "Equipe Renault") team.

Motor car race

The **1988 French Grand Prix** was a [Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One") motor race held on 3 July 1988 at the [Circuit Paul Ricard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_Paul_Ricard "Circuit Paul Ricard"), [Le Castellet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Castellet,_Var "Le Castellet, Var"). It was the seventh race of the [1988 Formula One World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Formula_One_World_Championship "1988 Formula One World Championship").

The 80-lap race was won by local driver [Alain Prost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost"), driving a [McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren "McLaren")-[Honda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_in_Formula_One "Honda in Formula One"), after he started from [pole position](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pole_position "Pole position"). Prost's Brazilian teammate [Ayrton Senna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna") finished second, with Italian [Michele Alboreto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Alboreto "Michele Alboreto") third in a [Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari").

## Qualifying

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1988_French_Grand_Prix&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Qualifying")]

The two [McLarens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_MP4/4 "McLaren MP4/4") lined up in their usual front row places, but, for the first time this season, [Alain Prost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost") was ahead of [Ayrton Senna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna"), the Frenchman beating the Brazilian by almost half a second to take his first pole since the [1986 Monaco Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Monaco_Grand_Prix "1986 Monaco Grand Prix") and in doing so stopping his teammate from a record-breaking 7th pole in succession. The two [Ferraris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrari_F1/87#F1/87/88C "Ferrari F1/87") filled the second row, [Gerhard Berger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerhard_Berger "Gerhard Berger") beating [Michele Alboreto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Alboreto "Michele Alboreto") by over 1.1 seconds, though neither driver believed they could race with the McLarens simply because of fuel consumption. On the third row were the two [normally-aspirated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naturally_aspirated_engine "Naturally aspirated engine")[Benettons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benetton_B188 "Benetton B188") of [Thierry Boutsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thierry_Boutsen "Thierry Boutsen") and [Alessandro Nannini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alessandro_Nannini "Alessandro Nannini"), while the [Lotuses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotus_100T "Lotus 100T") of [Nelson Piquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") and [Satoru Nakajima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satoru_Nakajima "Satoru Nakajima") filled the fourth row, Piquet being the last driver to qualify under 1:10. The top ten was completed by the [Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_FW12 "Williams FW12") of [Nigel Mansell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Mansell "Nigel Mansell") (over 2.7 seconds slower than Prost and almost 4 seconds slower than his [1987](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_French_Grand_Prix "1987 French Grand Prix") pole time) and the [March](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_881 "March 881") of [Ivan Capelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Capelli "Ivan Capelli"), who had recovered after fracturing his left foot in a crash during practice in [Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Detroit_Grand_Prix "1988 Detroit Grand Prix") two weeks before.

Meanwhile, [Ligier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equipe_Ligier "Equipe Ligier") had a disastrous weekend on their home turf with both [René Arnoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ren%C3%A9_Arnoux "René Arnoux"), a winner with [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_F1 "Renault F1") at the circuit in [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_French_Grand_Prix "1982 French Grand Prix"), and [Stefan Johansson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefan_Johansson "Stefan Johansson") failing to qualify, though they did have a celebration of sorts over the weekend as Arnoux turned 40 the day after the race. [Julian Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Bailey_(racing_driver) "Julian Bailey (racing driver)") also failed to qualify in his [Tyrrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrrell_017 "Tyrrell 017"), while [Piercarlo Ghinzani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piercarlo_Ghinzani "Piercarlo Ghinzani") qualified 22nd in his [Zakspeed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zakspeed_881 "Zakspeed 881") but was excluded for missing a weight check, thus promoting [Oscar Larrauri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Larrauri "Oscar Larrauri")'s [EuroBrun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EuroBrun_ER188 "EuroBrun ER188") to the last grid spot.

## Race summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1988_French_Grand_Prix&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Race summary")]

Prost led away from Senna and the two Ferraris, with Piquet passing the two Benettons for fifth. Despite worries in the McLaren pit about overly high fuel consumption (the fuel readouts in the cars were showing less fuel used than what the Honda telemetry was telling the team), Ron Dennis was reportedly prepared to let his drivers run out of fuel at the expense of a perfect season if it taught them to be more conservative given their obvious advantage over the field, though ultimately the onboard readouts were proved correct. Prost maintained a two-second advantage over Senna until the mid-race pit stops, while an early stop by Berger on lap 22 allowed teammate Alboreto through into third. While both McLarens were racing each other out front, they were still pulling away from the field at sometimes a second per lap.

Senna made his pit stop three laps before Prost, enabling him to take the lead thanks to a slow stop for Prost with a sticking front wheel, but traffic on the Mistral Straight (including a less than helpful Piquet who most likely enjoyed seeing Senna lose the lead to Prost at close quarters) and a gearbox problem allowed Prost to close right up to him and then overtake him on lap 61 as they lapped [Alex Caffi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Caffi "Alex Caffi") and [Pierluigi Martini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierluigi_Martini "Pierluigi Martini") at the Signes corner. Meanwhile, Berger reclaimed third only for Alboreto to pass him again during the pit stops, while Mansell suffered his seventh consecutive retirement, dropping out on lap 49 with suspension problems, though he had been dropping back for a number of laps with power loss from his [Judd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judd_(engine)#CV "Judd (engine)")[V8 engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V8_engine "V8 engine"). After returning to the pits and getting himself cleaned up, the Englishman left the circuit profoundly fed up with the performance of the Williams, fuelling ongoing speculation in the press that he would leave the team at the end of the year to join Ferrari after the Italian team had announced they would not be keeping Alboreto for 1989. Despite the rumours turning out to be correct, Mansell continued to deny he was joining Ferrari.

In the closing laps, Prost pulled away as Senna's gearbox troubles continued, losing several gears. The Brazilian eventually finished nearly 32 seconds behind the Frenchman, though he was still nearly 35 seconds ahead of Alboreto, the last man on the lead lap. Berger was fourth ahead of Piquet, who also suffered gearbox problems in the later stages of the race; the final point went to the Benetton of Nannini. France was the first time since the [1987 Monaco Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_Monaco_Grand_Prix "1987 Monaco Grand Prix") that Alboreto had finished in front of his teammate in a race where they both finished. During the race Alboreto had the advantage of an almost perfectly balanced car, while Berger complained of severe understeer, something not needed at the high speed Signes corner at the end of the Mistral.

The fastest lap of the race, a 1:11.737 set by Prost on lap 45, was over two seconds slower than the 1:09.548 set by Piquet in a Honda-powered Williams the [previous year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_French_Grand_Prix "1987 French Grand Prix") – a consequence of the restrictions imposed on [turbocharged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turbocharger "Turbocharger") engines this season with the major difference being the speeds attained on the now 1 km long Mistral Straight. In 1987 the fastest turbo cars (Honda powered) were timed at 325 km/h (202 mph) on the straight. In 1988 the top speed was recorded at 311 km/h (193 mph).

For Prost it was his third win in his home Grand Prix after winning in both [1981](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_French_Grand_Prix "1981 French Grand Prix") at [Dijon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dijon-Prenois "Dijon-Prenois") (his first Grand Prix victory) and [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_French_Grand_Prix "1983 French Grand Prix") at the full length Paul Ricard. On both occasions he had been driving for the factory [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equipe_Renault "Equipe Renault") team.

**Alain Prost won his 32nd F1 World Championship race at the 1988 French F1 GP. The McLaren driver started from pole and won on the Paul Ricard circuit for the second time. It was also his 4th win of the season and the 62nd win for the McLaren F1 team.**

## Prost's pole, Ligier's English ingredient

Paul Ricard 1988 produced two unexpected stories. The first was Prost taking pole position on both Friday and Saturday, his first since Hungary 1986, and breaking Ayrton Senna's six-race stranglehold on the front of the grid. On Friday he ran 1m 8.111s to Senna's 1m 8.456s; on Saturday he improved to 1m 7.589s. The Frenchman had spent the week between Detroit and the home race in deliberate preparation: chassis settings tuned to the long Mistral straight, fuel-mileage calculations balanced for downforce. For the first time all year, Senna sat second on the grid.

The off-track news was Ligier's. Frank Dernie, Patrick Head's deputy at Williams, had signed for Ligier on 24 June, a remarkable move that paired one of the best English engineers in the paddock with what Rene Arnoux had publicly called the worst Formula 1 car he had ever driven. Williams refused to release Dernie from his twelve-month notice clause; he would not arrive at Magny-Cours (where Guy Ligier was relocating from Abrest with help from Mitterrand's tax breaks) until summer 1989. Both Ligier cars failed to qualify at the team's home race. Harvey Postlethwaite resigned from Ferrari to join Tyrrell as technical director; John Barnard moved into pit-wall management at the Scuderia. Pier Giorgio Capelli was installed as Ferrari's new general manager. Marco Piccinini's position was being slowly retired in deference to Enzo Ferrari's failing health.

## Berger keeps up, then drops back

The Ferrari pair sat third (Berger) and fourth (Alboreto) on the grid, but Marco Piccinini admitted before the race that the team would run with low boost to make the fuel last; Berger and Alboreto would not be racing for the win. The Benetton-Fords occupied row three (Boutsen and Nannini, two seconds adrift of pole); the Lotus pair sat sixth and seventh on Honda V6s nearly identical to the McLarens but in chassis that gave nothing away to design but everything away to set-up.

Sunday's race opened with Prost rocketing away from pole. Berger surprised Senna at the start; the Brazilian dived inside at the first braking zone to retake second. The order at lap five was Prost, Senna by three seconds, Berger by seven, Alboreto by ten, Piquet by seventeen and the rest a single line of slower cars behind. By lap fourteen Berger was down to fifth with a Ferrari that was dropping pressure on every braking zone; he pitted for tyres on lap 22 and lost more places. Alboreto inherited third for Ferrari ahead of Piquet.

## The pit stops swap the order

Senna pitted on lap 34 for fresh Goodyears in 9s; Prost stayed out one lap longer and emerged behind Senna after a 10.6s stop with a sticky right-front nut. The McLaren had handed its lead to its team-mate. From lap 36 to lap 60 Senna held a steady 1.5-second cushion in front of Prost as the Frenchman waited for the moment to attempt a pass. The race became, in essence, a chess game over fuel mileage at the front and over the lapped traffic in the closing fifteen laps. Boutsen retired on lap 38 with an ignition problem; Patrese on lap 37 with a brake-balance failure; Mansell on lap 50 with a broken rear suspension wishbone.

The decisive moment came on lap 61. Senna and Prost arrived at the Beausset double-right behind the lapped Pierluigi Martini; Caffi tried to pass Martini on the inside, Martini took a wide line to defend, Senna got caught in the Minardi's turbulence and was carried off-line into the corner. Prost, who had held the inside, kept his line through the apex, picked up the slipstream out of Beausset and powered past both Martini and Senna into the next braking zone. The lead was his. Senna stayed on his gearbox for two more laps with a McLaren that had lost its second gear and was on emergency fuel-saving mode, then conceded.

## Prost in front of his home crowd, McLaren's seventh straight

Prost crossed the line 31.7 seconds ahead for his 32nd career grand prix victory, his third at Paul Ricard (after 1983) and his fourth at a French grand prix in his career, and McLaren-Honda's seventh consecutive 1988 win. Senna parked the second McLaren on the slowing-down lap, out of fuel. Alboreto took third for Ferrari, the only non-McLaren on the lead lap; Berger fourth, Piquet fifth, Nannini sixth. Ron Dennis surprised the protocol by climbing the podium during God Save the Queen, visibly aware that his team had now won seven consecutive grands prix, the longest such streak since the Ferrari 500 of the early 1950s.

"I think I chose the right settings everywhere," Prost said. "Maybe a tenth quicker than Senna. Our only worry today was tyres and fuel. I kept saving them. While waiting for the opportunity." The opportunity had been a Minardi at the Beausset, the kind of moment that, in Prost's hands, decided a grand prix and a championship. The Frenchman now led the table 54 to Senna's 39, fifteen points clear with eight rounds left. Ron Dennis's 16-from-16 dream was still alive. McLaren had 93 of a possible 112 constructor points. The summer races at Silverstone, Hockenheim, the Hungaroring and Spa would test whether the season was running out of variance.

**Alain Prost won his 32nd F1 World Championship race at the 1988 French F1 GP. The McLaren driver started from pole and won on the Paul Ricard circuit for the second time. It was also his 4th win of the season and the 62nd win for the McLaren F1 team.**

## Prost's pole, Ligier's English ingredient

Paul Ricard 1988 produced two unexpected stories. The first was Prost taking pole position on both Friday and Saturday, his first since Hungary 1986, and breaking Ayrton Senna's six-race stranglehold on the front of the grid. On Friday he ran 1m 8.111s to Senna's 1m 8.456s; on Saturday he improved to 1m 7.589s. The Frenchman had spent the week between Detroit and the home race in deliberate preparation: chassis settings tuned to the long Mistral straight, fuel-mileage calculations balanced for downforce. For the first time all year, Senna sat second on the grid.

The off-track news was Ligier's. Frank Dernie, Patrick Head's deputy at Williams, had signed for Ligier on 24 June, a remarkable move that paired one of the best English engineers in the paddock with what Rene Arnoux had publicly called the worst Formula 1 car he had ever driven. Williams refused to release Dernie from his twelve-month notice clause; he would not arrive at Magny-Cours (where Guy Ligier was relocating from Abrest with help from Mitterrand's tax breaks) until summer 1989. Both Ligier cars failed to qualify at the team's home race. Harvey Postlethwaite resigned from Ferrari to join Tyrrell as technical director; John Barnard moved into pit-wall management at the Scuderia. Pier Giorgio Capelli was installed as Ferrari's new general manager. Marco Piccinini's position was being slowly retired in deference to Enzo Ferrari's failing health.

## Berger keeps up, then drops back

The Ferrari pair sat third (Berger) and fourth (Alboreto) on the grid, but Marco Piccinini admitted before the race that the team would run with low boost to make the fuel last; Berger and Alboreto would not be racing for the win. The Benetton-Fords occupied row three (Boutsen and Nannini, two seconds adrift of pole); the Lotus pair sat sixth and seventh on Honda V6s nearly identical to the McLarens but in chassis that gave nothing away to design but everything away to set-up.

Sunday's race opened with Prost rocketing away from pole. Berger surprised Senna at the start; the Brazilian dived inside at the first braking zone to retake second. The order at lap five was Prost, Senna by three seconds, Berger by seven, Alboreto by ten, Piquet by seventeen and the rest a single line of slower cars behind. By lap fourteen Berger was down to fifth with a Ferrari that was dropping pressure on every braking zone; he pitted for tyres on lap 22 and lost more places. Alboreto inherited third for Ferrari ahead of Piquet.

## The pit stops swap the order

Senna pitted on lap 34 for fresh Goodyears in 9s; Prost stayed out one lap longer and emerged behind Senna after a 10.6s stop with a sticky right-front nut. The McLaren had handed its lead to its team-mate. From lap 36 to lap 60 Senna held a steady 1.5-second cushion in front of Prost as the Frenchman waited for the moment to attempt a pass. The race became, in essence, a chess game over fuel mileage at the front and over the lapped traffic in the closing fifteen laps. Boutsen retired on lap 38 with an ignition problem; Patrese on lap 37 with a brake-balance failure; Mansell on lap 50 with a broken rear suspension wishbone.

The decisive moment came on lap 61. Senna and Prost arrived at the Beausset double-right behind the lapped Pierluigi Martini; Caffi tried to pass Martini on the inside, Martini took a wide line to defend, Senna got caught in the Minardi's turbulence and was carried off-line into the corner. Prost, who had held the inside, kept his line through the apex, picked up the slipstream out of Beausset and powered past both Martini and Senna into the next braking zone. The lead was his. Senna stayed on his gearbox for two more laps with a McLaren that had lost its second gear and was on emergency fuel-saving mode, then conceded.

## Prost in front of his home crowd, McLaren's seventh straight

Prost crossed the line 31.7 seconds ahead for his 32nd career grand prix victory, his third at Paul Ricard (after 1983) and his fourth at a French grand prix in his career, and McLaren-Honda's seventh consecutive 1988 win. Senna parked the second McLaren on the slowing-down lap, out of fuel. Alboreto took third for Ferrari, the only non-McLaren on the lead lap; Berger fourth, Piquet fifth, Nannini sixth. Ron Dennis surprised the protocol by climbing the podium during God Save the Queen, visibly aware that his team had now won seven consecutive grands prix, the longest such streak since the Ferrari 500 of the early 1950s.

"I think I chose the right settings everywhere," Prost said. "Maybe a tenth quicker than Senna. Our only worry today was tyres and fuel. I kept saving them. While waiting for the opportunity." The opportunity had been a Minardi at the Beausset, the kind of moment that, in Prost's hands, decided a grand prix and a championship. The Frenchman now led the table 54 to Senna's 39, fifteen points clear with eight rounds left. Ron Dennis's 16-from-16 dream was still alive. McLaren had 93 of a possible 112 constructor points. The summer races at Silverstone, Hockenheim, the Hungaroring and Spa would test whether the season was running out of variance.

It had to happen. For the first six Grand Prix races of 1988 Alain Prost has appeared to be content to let his Brazilian team-mate set the pace, with blindingly quick qualifying laps that gave him six consecutive pole-positions. He agreed to Senna having first call on the McLaren-Honda T-car for those events, and when Senna had trouble in the race (as in Brazil) or crashed (as at Monaco) or got elbowed out at the start (as in Mexico) Prost eased serenely into the lead.

The score before the French Grand Prix was three wins each, but more impressive, and more important to the overall scene, was the fact that the McLaren-Honda MP4/4 cars had won six races out of six.

At the flat and featureless Paul Ricard circuit, on the arid plain in the mountains behind the Mediterranean coast-line between Toulon and Marseilles, Prost arrived with his name on the McLaren T-car and a very aggressive will to win at all costs – quite unlike the normally cool and placid Monsieur Prost.

It had to happen. For the first six Grand Prix races of 1988 Alain Prost has appeared to be content to let his Brazilian team-mate set the pace, with blindingly quick qualifying laps that gave him six consecutive pole-positions. He agreed to Senna having first call on the McLaren-Honda T-car for those events, and when Senna had trouble in the race (as in Brazil) or crashed (as at Monaco) or got elbowed out at the start (as in Mexico) Prost eased serenely into the lead.

The score before the French Grand Prix was three wins each, but more impressive, and more important to the overall scene, was the fact that the McLaren-Honda MP4/4 cars had won six races out of six.

At the flat and featureless Paul Ricard circuit, on the arid plain in the mountains behind the Mediterranean coast-line between Toulon and Marseilles, Prost arrived with his name on the McLaren T-car and a very aggressive will to win at all costs – quite unlike the normally cool and placid Monsieur Prost.

The **1988 French Grand Prix**, otherwise officially advertised as the **[74 e Rhône-Poulenc Grand Prix de France](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/French_Grand_Prix "French Grand Prix")**, was the seventh round of the [1988](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_Formula_One_Season "1988 Formula One Season")[FIA](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/FIA "FIA")[Formula One World Championship](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One"), staged at the [Circuit Paul Ricard](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Circuit_Paul_Ricard "Circuit Paul Ricard") in Le Castellet, France, on the [3 July](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/July_3 "July 3") 1988.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) The race would see [Alain Prost](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost") claim a dominant home [victory](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Victory "Victory") for [McLaren](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/McLaren_Racing "McLaren Racing")-[Honda](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Honda "Honda"), half a minute clear of teammate [Ayrton Senna](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna").[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

[Qualifying](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Qualifying "Qualifying") once again proved to be a McLaren-Honda benefit, although Prost cause something of an upset by beating Senna to [pole](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Pole "Pole"), with almost half a second between them.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) Best of the rest was [Gerhard Berger](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Gerhard_Berger "Gerhard Berger") in the #28 [Ferrari](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari"), two tenths off of Senna, while [Michele Alboreto](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Michele_Alboreto "Michele Alboreto") was over a second slower than his teammate in fourth.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

Prost duly beat Senna off the line to claim the lead at the start, while [Nelson Piquet](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") charged through from seventh to challenge the Ferraris.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) The defending Champion ultimately had to slot his [Lotus](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Team_Lotus "Team Lotus") in behind Alboreto, however, a shuffle which allowed both Prost and Senna to ease clear during the opening lap.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

Indeed, in a repeat of their performance from [Canada](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_Canadian_Grand_Prix "1988 Canadian Grand Prix") the two McLarens worked together during the early stages, pulling out a sizeable lead. Behind, Berger would be forced to concede third to his teammate Alboreto by making an early stop, with the pair still being harassed by Piquet.

Senna would make his mid-race stop for tyres three laps earlier than Prost, and duly managed to take the lead as the Frenchman lost time with a sticking wheel.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) The Brazilian subsequently established a small lead, although a gearbox issue for Senna saw his pace gradually drop off.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

Yet, Prost was still unable to make a move on his teammate, and would have to wait until the pair came to lap a stubborn Piquet to retake the lead.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) Prost subsequently eased ahead as Senna's gearbox issues worsened, opening out a thirty second advantage before the end of the race.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

Indeed, there were no further changes to the order after Prost's pass, with the Frenchman extending his Championship lead with his fourth win of the season. Senna limped home in second, still half a minute ahead of Alboreto, with Berger, Piquet and [Alessandro Nannini](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Alessandro_Nannini "Alessandro Nannini") claiming the remaining points.

## Background[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Ff1.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2F1988_French_Grand_Prix%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D1&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

[Alain Prost](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost") had seen his lead reduced by teammate [Ayrton Senna](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna") in Detroit last time out, although the Frenchman still held a healthy twelve point advantage. Those two were in a class of their own at the head of the field, with Senna fifteen clear of third placed [Gerhard Berger](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Gerhard_Berger "Gerhard Berger"), already making the Austrian an outsider for the Championship. Elsewhere, [Thierry Boutsen](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Thierry_Boutsen "Thierry Boutsen") had moved ahead of [Nelson Piquet](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") to claim fifth in Detroit, with fifteen drivers on the score board.

It was also pure domination in the Constructors' Championship, with [McLaren](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/McLaren_Racing "McLaren Racing")-[Honda](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Honda "Honda") having moved onto 78 points after their fourth one-two of the season in the US. They hence left Detroit with a 51 point lead, more than three races worth of points, with [Ferrari](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari") still their largest threat in second. Elsewhere, [Benetton](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Benetton_Formula "Benetton Formula")-[Ford](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Ford "Ford")[Cosworth](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Cosworth "Cosworth") had moved ahead of [Lotus](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Team_Lotus "Team Lotus")-[Honda](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Honda "Honda") on count-back, and hence claimed third, while [Arrows](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Arrows "Arrows")-[Megatron](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Megatron "Megatron") retained their spot in the top five.

The **1988 French Grand Prix**, otherwise officially advertised as the **[74 e Rhône-Poulenc Grand Prix de France](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/French_Grand_Prix "French Grand Prix")**, was the seventh round of the [1988](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_Formula_One_Season "1988 Formula One Season")[FIA](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/FIA "FIA")[Formula One World Championship](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One"), staged at the [Circuit Paul Ricard](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Circuit_Paul_Ricard "Circuit Paul Ricard") in Le Castellet, France, on the [3 July](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/July_3 "July 3") 1988.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) The race would see [Alain Prost](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost") claim a dominant home [victory](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Victory "Victory") for [McLaren](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/McLaren_Racing "McLaren Racing")-[Honda](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Honda "Honda"), half a minute clear of teammate [Ayrton Senna](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna").[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

[Qualifying](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Qualifying "Qualifying") once again proved to be a McLaren-Honda benefit, although Prost cause something of an upset by beating Senna to [pole](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Pole "Pole"), with almost half a second between them.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) Best of the rest was [Gerhard Berger](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Gerhard_Berger "Gerhard Berger") in the #28 [Ferrari](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari"), two tenths off of Senna, while [Michele Alboreto](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Michele_Alboreto "Michele Alboreto") was over a second slower than his teammate in fourth.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

Prost duly beat Senna off the line to claim the lead at the start, while [Nelson Piquet](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") charged through from seventh to challenge the Ferraris.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) The defending Champion ultimately had to slot his [Lotus](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Team_Lotus "Team Lotus") in behind Alboreto, however, a shuffle which allowed both Prost and Senna to ease clear during the opening lap.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

Indeed, in a repeat of their performance from [Canada](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_Canadian_Grand_Prix "1988 Canadian Grand Prix") the two McLarens worked together during the early stages, pulling out a sizeable lead. Behind, Berger would be forced to concede third to his teammate Alboreto by making an early stop, with the pair still being harassed by Piquet.

Senna would make his mid-race stop for tyres three laps earlier than Prost, and duly managed to take the lead as the Frenchman lost time with a sticking wheel.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) The Brazilian subsequently established a small lead, although a gearbox issue for Senna saw his pace gradually drop off.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

Yet, Prost was still unable to make a move on his teammate, and would have to wait until the pair came to lap a stubborn Piquet to retake the lead.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1) Prost subsequently eased ahead as Senna's gearbox issues worsened, opening out a thirty second advantage before the end of the race.[[1]](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/1988_French_Grand_Prix#cite_note-GP-1)

Indeed, there were no further changes to the order after Prost's pass, with the Frenchman extending his Championship lead with his fourth win of the season. Senna limped home in second, still half a minute ahead of Alboreto, with Berger, Piquet and [Alessandro Nannini](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Alessandro_Nannini "Alessandro Nannini") claiming the remaining points.

## Background[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Ff1.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2F1988_French_Grand_Prix%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D1&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

[Alain Prost](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Alain_Prost "Alain Prost") had seen his lead reduced by teammate [Ayrton Senna](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna") in Detroit last time out, although the Frenchman still held a healthy twelve point advantage. Those two were in a class of their own at the head of the field, with Senna fifteen clear of third placed [Gerhard Berger](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Gerhard_Berger "Gerhard Berger"), already making the Austrian an outsider for the Championship. Elsewhere, [Thierry Boutsen](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Thierry_Boutsen "Thierry Boutsen") had moved ahead of [Nelson Piquet](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") to claim fifth in Detroit, with fifteen drivers on the score board.

It was also pure domination in the Constructors' Championship, with [McLaren](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/McLaren_Racing "McLaren Racing")-[Honda](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Honda "Honda") having moved onto 78 points after their fourth one-two of the season in the US. They hence left Detroit with a 51 point lead, more than three races worth of points, with [Ferrari](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari") still their largest threat in second. Elsewhere, [Benetton](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Benetton_Formula "Benetton Formula")-[Ford](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Ford "Ford")[Cosworth](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Cosworth "Cosworth") had moved ahead of [Lotus](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Team_Lotus "Team Lotus")-[Honda](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Honda "Honda") on count-back, and hence claimed third, while [Arrows](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Arrows "Arrows")-[Megatron](https://f1.fandom.com/wiki/Megatron "Megatron") retained their spot in the top five.
